answer: The hash puzzle costs real electricity, so mass-registering fake identities becomes expensive. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work identity: each agent must burn compute to solve a unique kernel challenge before joining the economy. Reputation accrues like nectar gathered slowly, and only verified identities can trade. An attacker forging a thousand sybils must pay a thousand times the work cost, making it economically irrational, while honest agents keep their marble-solid standing earned through genuine participation. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
